newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy welcomes Eurostat decision on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy welcomes Eurostat decision on EMU.

text.p: Italy said on Monday a ruling by the European Union's statistical office, Eurostat, meant the European Commission's forecast of its 1997 deficit-to-gross domestic product ratio had fallen from 3.3 percent to 3.0 percent.
The 3.0-percent level, if achieved, would help Italy qualify for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The Treasury issued a statement welcoming the Eurostat ruling after the body approved Italian methods of calculating interest on postal bonds and zero-coupon bonds.

"The Brussels Commission, in its forecasts for 1997, attributed to Italy a deficit-to-GDP ratio of 3.3 percent...only in so far as a decision was outstanding from Eurostat on certain reclassification measures, which would make the deficit-GDP ratio 3.0 percent. That is what happened today," the statement said.
"The positive and definitive decision by Eurostat clearly demonstrates that Italy has not adopted any measures to embellish its accounting nor intends to do so in the future," the statement said.
